Wyoming and Utah have submitted Regional Haze State Implementation Plans with no proposed pollution reductions, allowing some of the nation's biggest polluters to remain uncontrolled for nitrogen oxide, sulfur dioxide, and other pollutants when common-sense controls exist that could significantly cut those emissions.
EPAs proposed disapprovals of these do-nothing state plans are a critical first step to protect air quality, both in national parks and our communities. I urge EPA to finalize its proposed disapprovals and act quickly to implement plans that will result in real pollution reductions.
In Utah, EPA analysis shows that installing selective catalytic reduction (SCR) on Hunter and Huntington coal plants would be cost-effective and provide massive visibility benefits for Utahs national parks. These plants have avoided pollution reductions for decades. Now is the time for EPA to act.
Similarly, in Wyoming, the state failed to even consider pollution controls at the states largest polluters, including Jim Bridger, Naughton, Dave Johnston, and Wyodak coal plants. Each of these facilities could install cost-effective pollution controls, including SCRs, that would result in significant air-quality improvements across the state.
Please finalize the proposed disapprovals of Utah and Wyomings do-nothing plans and require enforceable pollution reductions, including SCR installation, on our states' biggest polluters Hunter, Huntington, Jim Bridger, Naughton, Dave Johnston, and Wyodak.

EPAs proposed disapprovals of these do-nothing state plans are a critical first step to protect air quality, both in national parks and our communities. I urge EPA to finalize its proposed disapprovals and act quickly to implement plans that will result in real pollution reductions.
In Utah, EPA analysis shows that installing selective catalytic reduction (SCR) on Hunter and Huntington coal plants would be cost-effective and provide massive visibility benefits for Utahs national parks. These plants have avoided pollution reductions for decades. Now is the time for EPA to act.
Similarly, in Wyoming, the state failed to even consider pollution controls at the states largest polluters, including Jim Bridger, Naughton, Dave Johnston, and Wyodak coal plants. Each of these facilities could install cost-effective pollution controls, including SCRs, that would result in significant air-quality improvements across the state.
Please finalize the proposed disapprovals of Utah and Wyomings do-nothing plans and require enforceable pollution reductions, including SCR installation, on our states' biggest polluters Hunter, Huntington, Jim Bridger, Naughton, Dave Johnston, and Wyodak.

Wyoming and Utah have submitted Regional Haze State Implementation Plans with no proposed pollution reductions, allowing some of the nation's biggest polluters to remain uncontrolled for nitrogen oxide, sulfur dioxide, and other pollutants when common-sense controls exist that could significantly cut those emissions.
EPAs proposed disapprovals of these do-nothing state plans are a critical first step to protect air quality, both in national parks and our communities. I urge EPA to finalize its proposed disapprovals and act quickly to implement plans that will result in real pollution reductions.
In Utah, EPA analysis shows that installing selective catalytic reduction (SCR) on Hunter and Huntington coal plants would be cost-effective and provide massive visibility benefits for Utahs national parks. These plants have avoided pollution reductions for decades. Now is the time for EPA to act.
Similarly, in Wyoming, the state failed to even consider pollution controls at the states largest polluters, including Jim Bridger, Naughton, Dave Johnston, and Wyodak coal plants. Each of these facilities could install cost-effective pollution controls, including SCRs, that would result in significant air-quality improvements across the state.
Please finalize the proposed disapprovals of Utah and Wyomings do-nothing plans and require enforceable pollution reductions, including SCR installation, on our states' biggest polluters Hunter, Huntington, Jim Bridger, Naughton, Dave Johnston, and Wyodak.

Wyoming and Utah have submitted Regional Haze State Implementation Plans with no proposed pollution reductions, allowing some of the nation's biggest polluters to remain uncontrolled for nitrogen oxide, sulfur dioxide, and other pollutants when common-sense controls exist that could significantly cut those emissions.
EPAs proposed disapprovals of these do-nothing state plans are a critical first step to protect air quality, both in national parks and our communities. I urge EPA to finalize its proposed disapprovals and act quickly to implement plans that will result in real pollution reductions.
In Utah, EPA analysis shows that installing selective catalytic reduction (SCR) on Hunter and Huntington coal plants would be cost-effective and provide massive visibility benefits for Utahs national parks. These plants have avoided pollution reductions for decades. Now is the time for EPA to act.
Similarly, in Wyoming, the state failed to even consider pollution controls at the states largest polluters, including Jim Bridger, Naughton, Dave Johnston, and Wyodak coal plants. Each of these facilities could install cost-effective pollution controls, including SCRs, that would result in significant air-quality improvements across the state.
Please finalize the proposed disapprovals of Utah and Wyomings do-nothing plans and require enforceable pollution reductions, including SCR installation, on our states' biggest polluters Hunter, Huntington, Jim Bridger, Naughton, Dave Johnston, and Wyodak.

Wyoming and Utah have submitted Regional Haze State Implementation Plans with no proposed pollution reductions, allowing some of the nation's biggest polluters to remain uncontrolled for nitrogen oxide, sulfur dioxide, and other pollutants when common-sense controls exist that could significantly cut those emissions.
EPAs proposed disapprovals of these do-nothing state plans are a critical first step to protect air quality, both in national parks and our communities. I urge EPA to finalize its proposed disapprovals and act quickly to implement plans that will result in real pollution reductions.
In Utah, EPA analysis shows that installing selective catalytic reduction (SCR) on Hunter and Huntington coal plants would be cost-effective and provide massive visibility benefits for Utahs national parks. These plants have avoided pollution reductions for decades. Now is the time for EPA to act.
Similarly, in Wyoming, the state failed to even consider pollution controls at the states largest polluters, including Jim Bridger, Naughton, Dave Johnston, and Wyodak coal plants. Each of these facilities could install cost-effective pollution controls, including SCRs, that would result in significant air-quality improvements across the state.
Please finalize the proposed disapprovals of Utah and Wyomings do-nothing plans and require enforceable pollution reductions, including SCR installation, on our states' biggest polluters Hunter, Huntington, Jim Bridger, Naughton, Dave Johnston, and Wyodak.

EPAs proposed disapprovals of these do-nothing state plans are a critical first step to protect air quality, both in national parks and our communities. I urge EPA to finalize its proposed disapprovals and act quickly to implement plans that will result in real pollution reductions.
In Utah, EPA analysis shows that installing selective catalytic reduction (SCR) on Hunter and Huntington coal plants would be cost-effective and provide massive visibility benefits for Utahs national parks. These plants have avoided pollution reductions for decades. Now is the time for EPA to act.
Similarly, in Wyoming, the state failed to even consider pollution controls at the states largest polluters, including Jim Bridger, Naughton, Dave Johnston, and Wyodak coal plants. Each of these facilities could install cost-effective pollution controls, including SCRs, that would result in significant air-quality improvements across the state.
Please finalize the proposed disapprovals of Utah and Wyomings do-nothing plans and require enforceable pollution reductions, including SCR installation, on our states' biggest polluters Hunter, Huntington, Jim Bridger, Naughton, Dave Johnston, and Wyodak.

Wyoming and Utah have submitted Regional Haze State Implementation Plans with no proposed pollution reductions, allowing some of the nation's biggest polluters to remain uncontrolled for nitrogen oxide, sulfur dioxide, and other pollutants when common-sense controls exist that could significantly cut those emissions.
EPAs proposed disapprovals of these do-nothing state plans are a critical first step to protect air quality, both in national parks and our communities. I urge EPA to finalize its proposed disapprovals and act quickly to implement plans that will result in real pollution reductions.
In Utah, EPA analysis shows that installing selective catalytic reduction (SCR) on Hunter and Huntington coal plants would be cost-effective and provide massive visibility benefits for Utahs national parks. These plants have avoided pollution reductions for decades. Now is the time for EPA to act.
Similarly, in Wyoming, the state failed to even consider pollution controls at the states largest polluters, including Jim Bridger, Naughton, Dave Johnston, and Wyodak coal plants. Each of these facilities could install cost-effective pollution controls, including SCRs, that would result in significant air-quality improvements across the state.
Please finalize the proposed disapprovals of Utah and Wyomings do-nothing plans and require enforceable pollution reductions, including SCR installation, on our states' biggest polluters Hunter, Huntington, Jim Bridger, Naughton, Dave Johnston, and Wyodak.

Wyoming and Utah have submitted Regional Haze State Implementation Plans with no proposed pollution reductions, allowing some of the nation's biggest polluters to remain uncontrolled for nitrogen oxide, sulfur dioxide, and other pollutants when common-sense controls exist that could significantly cut those emissions.
EPAs proposed disapprovals of these do-nothing state plans are a critical first step to protect air quality, both in national parks and our communities. I urge EPA to finalize its proposed disapprovals and act quickly to implement plans that will result in real pollution reductions.
In Utah, EPA analysis shows that installing selective catalytic reduction (SCR) on Hunter and Huntington coal plants would be cost-effective and provide massive visibility benefits for Utahs national parks. These plants have avoided pollution reductions for decades. Now is the time for EPA to act.
Similarly, in Wyoming, the state failed to even consider pollution controls at the states largest polluters, including Jim Bridger, Naughton, Dave Johnston, and Wyodak coal plants. Each of these facilities could install cost-effective pollution controls, including SCRs, that would result in significant air-quality improvements across the state.
Please finalize the proposed disapprovals of Utah and Wyomings do-nothing plans and require enforceable pollution reductions, including SCR installation, on our states' biggest polluters Hunter, Huntington, Jim Bridger, Naughton, Dave Johnston, and Wyodak.

Similarly, in Wyoming, the state failed to even consider pollution controls at the states largest polluters, including Jim Bridger, Naughton, Dave Johnston, and Wyodak coal plants. Each of these facilities could install cost-effective pollution controls, including SCRs, that would result in significant air-quality improvements across the state.
